Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an) on surah 97, verse 1:

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Tafsir of Surat al-Qadr

It is Madani.

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, We sent it down during the Night of Decree﴾. That is, the Qur'an. We have already mentioned that Allah the Exalted sent down the whole Qur'an during the Night of Decree to the lowest heaven, then sent it down to the Messenger piecemeal, one part after another. The pronoun (al-ha') refers back to the Qur'an, even though the Qur'an has not been mentioned, and this is valid because it is known.

And Laylat al-Qadr (the Night of Decree): it is the Night of Judgement (laylat al-hukm).

Mujahid said in the tafsir: Allah the Exalted apportions in it [the provisions] and the deeds.

They differed concerning the Night of Decree. It has been related from some of them that it was lifted when the Prophet died, but this is not correct; rather, it remains until the Hour is established.

And from Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: it is in the whole year, and whoever stands in prayer for a whole year will attain it.

The correct view is that it is in the last ten nights of Ramadan. This is established by the narration of Zirr ibn Hubaysh, that he said to Ubayy ibn Ka'b: "Your brother Abdullah ibn Mas'ud says that it is in the whole year." Ubayy ibn Ka'b said: "May Allah have mercy on Abu Abd al-Rahman! He knew that it is in the last ten nights of Ramadan, and he knew that it is the twenty-seventh night, but he wanted people not to rely on that." Then Ubayy ibn Ka'b swore, without making an exception, that it is the twenty-seventh night. Zirr said: "When I saw him swear, I said: O Abu al-Mundhir, how do you know that?" He said: "By the sign which the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) told us of, namely that the sun rises on its morning without its rays."

It is also established from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "Seek it in the last odd nights of Ramadan."

That is: search for it. In some narrations: "Seek it in the odd nights." In the narration of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri: "It is the night of the twenty-first."

It has been said otherwise, and the most correct and well-known of the opinions is that it is the night of the twenty-seventh, and whoever stands in prayer for the last ten nights will certainly and truly attain it.

And His saying: ﴿And what will make you know what the Night of Decree is?﴾ We have already explained that whatever occurs in the Qur'an in this form, "and what will make you know," Allah the Exalted has in fact informed him of it.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an) on surah 97, verse 3:

And His saying: ﴿The Night of Decree is better than a thousand months﴾ means: the reward for deeds performed in it is greater than the reward for deeds performed in a thousand months that do not include the Night of Decree (laylat al-qadr). Abu 'Isa al-Tirmidhi mentioned in his Jami', through the narration of Yusuf ibn Sa'd, that when al-Hasan ibn 'Ali (may Allah be pleased with them both) pledged allegiance to Mu'awiya and handed over the caliphate to him, a man said to him: "O you who blacken the faces of the believers!" or "O you who humiliate the believers!" He said: "Do not say that, for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was shown the Banu Umayya on his minbar, and that displeased him. So Allah the Exalted revealed to him: ﴿Indeed, We have granted you al-Kawthar﴾, and He also revealed: ﴿Indeed, We sent it down during the Night of Decree﴾, and He said: ﴿The Night of Decree is better than a thousand months﴾, meaning: better than a thousand months in which the Banu Umayya will rule."

Abu 'Isa said: "And it is gharib (strange)."

In some tafsir works it is reported that the Prophet said: "A man from the Children of Israel fought the enemies of Allah for a thousand months, and along with that he would stand in prayer at night and fast by day. He was saddened by this on account of the shortness of his community's lifespans and the fewness of their deeds. So Allah the Exalted revealed this surah and informed him that He had given them a night in which the deed would be better than the deed of that man for a thousand months."

It is also established concerning its virtue, from the Prophet (ﷺ), that he said: "Whoever stands in prayer on the Night of Decree out of faith and seeking reward, his previous sins will be forgiven."

Translation:

And His saying: ﴿The angels and the Spirit descend therein﴾ — i.e., Jibril (Gabriel) is among them, descending therein.

And His saying: ﴿By the permission of their Lord, for every matter﴾ — i.e., for every matter, which is what we mentioned of the decrees of things.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 97, verse 5:

As for His words ﴿Peace it is﴾, there are two opinions concerning it.

The first: what is meant by it is the greeting of peace from the angels to whoever remembers God Most High on that night.

The second opinion: ﴿Peace﴾ means safety (salama), and the meaning is that no sickness, no sorcery, and nothing of the works of the devils and soothsayers can take effect in it.

As for His words ﴿until the rising of the dawn﴾, it has been recited as "maṭli' al-fajr" with a kasra on the lam. So with a fatha it is a verbal noun (maṣdar), and with a kasra it denotes the time of rising.
